<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par75 />3rd pers. {{GHGheb|text=וַיִּרְאֶה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=18|verse=28}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=42|verse=16}} ''Q<sup>e</sup>re''; {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּֽעֲשֶׂה|translate=and he made}}, four times (but {{GHGheb|text=וַיַּ֫עַשׂ}} over 200 times); cf. also {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=19|verse=2}} ({{GHGheb|text=וַתִּזְנֶה}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=10|verse=29}} ({{GHGheb|text=וַתַּֽעֲלֶה}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=1|verse=16}} ({{GHGheb|text=וָֽאֲצַוֶּה}}), and {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=48}}. So also occasionally for the {{GHGterm|jussive}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=1|verse=9}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=34|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=28|verse=6}}.—For the well attested, but meaningless {{GHGheb|text=תִּֽירְאוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=6|verse=21}} (doubtless caused by the following {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּירָֽאוּ}}), read {{GHGheb|text=תִּרְאוּ|translate=ye see}}, with Ginsburg.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|u}}
4. The original {{GHGheb|text=י}} sometimes appears even before afformatives beginning with a vowel (cf. above, h and l), especially in and before the {{GHGterm|pause}}, and before the full plural ending {{GHGheb|text=־וּן}}, or where for any reason an emphasis rests on the word. {{GHGterm|Perfect}} {{GHGheb|text=חָסָ֫יָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=57|verse=2}}, {{GHGheb|text=חָסָ֫יוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=37}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=73|verse=2}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}; {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=בְּעָ֫יוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=12}}. {{GHGterm|Imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יֶאֱֽתָ֑יוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=16|verse=22}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=30|verse=14|hidebook=1}} (without the {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=68|verse=32}}); {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁלָ֫יוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=122|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=12|verse=6}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=77|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=יִרְבְּיֻן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=8|verse=13}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=36|verse=9}}: more frequently like {{GHGheb|text=יִשְׁתָּיוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=78|verse=44}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=17|verse=12}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=21|verse=12|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=11|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=31|verse=3|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=33|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=5|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=36|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=39|verse=7|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=83|verse=3|hidebook=1}}; before a suffix, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=3|verse=25}}. Also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=26|verse=7}} {{GHGheb|text=דָּֽלְיוּ}}, as ''perf. Qal'' from {{GHGheb|text=דָּלָה}}, was perhaps originally intended, but hardly {{GHGheb|text=דָּלָ֫יוּ}}, since these full forms, though they may stand out of pause, do not begin sentences; {{GHGheb|text=דַּ֫לְיוּ}} probably points to {{GHGheb|text=דַּ֫לּוּ}} from {{GHGheb|text=דָּלַל}} as the right reading, since the sense requires an intransitive verb. Cf. further, v, x, dd, gg.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|v}}
5. The {{GHGterm|participle active}} (cf. Vollers, ‘Das Qâtil-Partizipium,’ {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZA.|Zeitschrift für Assyriologie und verwandte Gebiete, ed. by C. Bezold. Lpz. 18S6 ff.}}}} 1903, p. 312 ff., and on the participles of {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}}, ''ibid.'', p. 316 ff.), besides feminine forms like {{GHGheb|text=עֹלָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=20|verse=31}}, &c., {{GHGheb|text=רֹאָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=20|verse=12}}, has also a ''feminine'' which retains the 3rd radical {{GHGheb|text=י}}, viz. {{GHGheb|text=בּֽוֹכִיָּה}} ( ={{GHGheb|text=בֹּכָה}}) ''weeping'', {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=הֽוֹמִיָּה|translate=tumultuous}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=22|verse=2}} (''plur.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=1|verse=21}}); {{GHGheb|text=צֽוֹפִיָּה|translate=spying}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=31|verse=27}}, {{GHGheb|text=פֹּֽרִיָּה|translate=fruitful}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=128|verse=3}}, ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=אֹֽתִיּוֹת|translate=the things that are to come}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=41|verse=23}}. With the ordinary strong inflexion {{GHGheb|text=י}} appears in {{GHGheb|text=עֹֽטְיָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=7}}, but perhaps there also {{GHGheb|text=עֹֽטִיָּה}} was intended, unless it should be {{GHGheb|text=טֹֽעִיָּה|translate=a wanderer}}. For {{GHGheb|text=רֹאָ֫נִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=47|verse=10}}, {{GHGheb|text=רֹאֵ֫נִי}} is to be read.—On {{GHGheb|text=עֹשֵׂה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=20|verse=40}} for {{GHGheb|text=עֹשֶׂה}}, cf. {{GHGpar|116|g}}, note.—In the {{GHGterm|participle passive}} the 3rd radical still sometimes appears as {{GHGheb|text=ו}} ({{GHGpar|24|b}}), cf. {{GHGheb|text=עָשׂוּ|translate=made}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=41|verse=25}}, {{GHGheb|text=צָפוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=15|verse=22}}, contracted from {{GHGheb|text=עָשׂוּו}}, {{GHGheb|text=צָפוּו}}; and before a formative ending, it even has its consonantal sound, {{GHGheb|text=העשוום}} (read {{GHGheb|text=הָֽעֲשׂוּוִם}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=23|verse=4}}; {{GHGheb|text=עשוות}} (read ''ʿ<sup>a</sup>sûwôth'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=18}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}, {{GHGheb|text=נטוות}} (read ''n<sup>e</sup>ṭûwôth'') {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=16}} {{GHGterm|K<sup>e</sup>thîbh}}. The shortening of the ''û'' in {{GHGheb|text=רְאֻיּוֹת}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Est|chapter=2|verse=9}} is irregular.

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|w}}
6. The defective writing is rare in such forms as {{GHGheb|text=וְהָיִ֫תָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=15|verse=33}}; {{GHGheb|text=בָּנִ֫תִי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=8|verse=44}}, cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=9|verse=3}}; {{GHGheb|text=וַתִּדְלֶ֫נָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=2|verse=16}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=18|verse=21}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=48|verse=6|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=7|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=5}}, &c.), and the pronunciation {{GHGheb|text=תִּרְאֶ֫ינָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=7|verse=10}}, cf. {{GHGheb|text=תַּֽעֲנֶ֑נָּה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=29}} (unless they are ''sing.'' with ''suff.'' of the 3rd ''sing. fem.''). Both cases are probably to be explained according to {{GHGpar|20|i}}.

{{center|II. ''On Niphʿal''.}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|75|x}}
7. Here the forms with {{GHGheb|text=־ֵי}} in the 1st and 2nd ''pers. sing.'' of the {{GHGterm|perfect}} predominate ({{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} only in {{GHGheb|text=נִקִּ֫יתָ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=8}}); on the other hand in the 1st ''plur'', always {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}}, as {{GHGheb|text=נִגְלִ֫ינוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=8}}. No examples of the 2nd ''plur.'' occur.—With {{GHGheb|text=י}} retained in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=נִטָּ֔יוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=24|verse=6}}; once with an initial guttural {{GHGheb|text=נִֽחֲרוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=1|verse=6}} for {{GHGheb|text=נֶֽחֱרוּ}}, probably arising from the ordinary strong form ''niḥru'', but the harshness of {{GHGheb|text=ח}} immediately followed by {{GHGheb|text=ר}} is avoided by pronouncing the {{GHGheb|text=ח}} with {{GHGterm|Ḥaṭeph-Pathaḥ}}.—In the 3rd ''sing. fem.'' {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁתָּֽוָה}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=27|verse=15}} (in {{GHGterm|pause}} for {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁתְּוָה}}) {{GHGheb|text=ו}} and {{GHGheb|text=ת}} may be transposed for euphonic reasons; but probably we should simply read {{GHGheb|text=נִשְׁוָ֫תָה}}.—Among Niphʿal forms of {{GHGheb|text=ל״ה}} must be classed, with Buxtorf and<section end=par75 /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
